voices.note: anonymous redactorial voice of this sugya
the תניא נמי הכי at 116a.14 on the practice in R' Eliezer's and R' Yosei HaGelili's locales

props.gloss_en: R' Akiva: [the meat of] a wild animal [in milk] is not [forbidden] by Torah law
R' Akiva: [the meat of] fowl [in milk] is not [forbidden] by Torah law
R' Yosei HaGelili: 'in its mother's milk' -- fowl is excluded, for it has no mother's milk
[what is between R' Yosei HaGelili and R' Akiva?] between them is a wild animal
R' Yosei HaGelili holds [the ban on] a wild animal [in milk] is Torah law
and R' Akiva holds [the ban on] a wild animal [in milk] is rabbinic
if you wish, say: between them is fowl
R' Akiva holds wild animal and fowl are not from the Torah -- but rabbinically they are forbidden
and R' Yosei HaGelili holds fowl [in milk] is not forbidden even rabbinically
in R' Eliezer's locale they would cut wood to make charcoal to make iron
in R' Yosei HaGelili's locale they would eat fowl meat in milk
Levi happened to come to the house of Yosef the fowler; they brought before him a peacock's head in milk, and he said nothing at all to them
when he came before Rebbi, [Rebbi] said to him: why did you not place them under a ban?
Levi: it is R' Yehuda ben Beteira's place, and I said [to myself]: he expounded for them in accordance with R' Yosei HaGelili
